32875-ten-years-captivity-in-the-mahdi-s.title: Delen, In Kordofan
32875-ten-years-captivity-in-the-mahdi-s.creator: Major F. R. Wingate, R.A.
32875-ten-years-captivity-in-the-mahdi-s.description: A book by Major F. R. Wingate, R.A.. Having but recently completed a _resumé_ of these events,[A] which had been largely compiled from the statements of natives who had escaped, I was not unnaturally desirous to verify, by the independent witness of Father Ohrwalder, the accounts which they had given, and I further begged Father Ohrwalder to carefully read over the book and point out the errors.

67357-the-missionary-sheriff-being-incid.title: Who Tried To Do His Duty_
67357-the-missionary-sheriff-being-incid.creator: Octave Thanet
67357-the-missionary-sheriff-being-incid.description: A book by Octave Thanet. Above the jail the street is a pretty street, with trim cottages and lawns and gardens; below, the sky-lines dwindle ignobly into shabby one and two story wooden shops devoted to the humbler handicrafts. It is not a street favored by processions; only the little soldiers of the Orphans’ Home Company would choose to tramp over its unkempt macadam.

arxiv-2111-03357.title: Sterile neutrinos with neutrino telescopes
arxiv-2111-03357.creator: Carlos A. Argüelles, Jordi Salvado
arxiv-2111-03357.description: Abstract Searches for light sterile neutrinos are motivated by the unexpected observation of electron neutrino appearance in short-baseline experiments, such as the Liquid Scintillator Neutrino Detector (LSND) and the Mini Booster Neutrino Experiment (MiniBooNE). In light of these unexpected results, a campaign using natural and anthropogenic sources to find light—mass-squared-difference around 1 eV 2 —sterile neutrinos is underway.

arxiv-2209-06369.title: Data-Driven Machine Learning Models for a Multi-Objective Flapping Fin Unmanned Underwater Vehicle Control System Preprint
arxiv-2209-06369.creator: Julian Lee, Kamal Viswanath, Jason Geder, Alisha Sharma, Marius Pruessner, Brian Zhou
arxiv-2209-06369.description: Abstract Flapping-fin unmanned underwater vehicle (UUV) propulsion systems provide high maneuverability for naval tasks such as surveillance and terrain exploration. Recent work has explored the use of time-series neural network surrogate models to predict thrust from vehicle design and fin kinematics. We develop a search-based inverse model that leverages a kinematics-to-thrust neural network model for control system design.

arxiv-2211-05914.title: Integrability and BRST invariance from BF topological theory
arxiv-2211-05914.creator: A. Restuccia and A. Sotomayor
arxiv-2211-05914.description: Abstract We consider the BRST invariant effective action of the non-abelian BF topological theory in 1 + 1 1+1 dimensions with gauge group S ​ l ​ ( 2 , ℝ ) Sl(2,\mathbb{R}) . By considering different gauge fixing conditions, the zero-curvature field equation give rise to several well known integrable equations.

arxiv-2211-16064.title: Locating the source of forced oscillations in transmission power grids
arxiv-2211-16064.creator: Robin Delabays 1 , Andrey Y. Lokhov 2 , Melvyn Tyloo 2,3 , Marc Vuffray 2
arxiv-2211-16064.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Robin Delabays 1 , Andrey Y. Lokhov 2 , Melvyn Tyloo 2,3 , Marc Vuffray 2. Forced oscillation event in power grids refers to a state where malfunctioning or abnormally operating equipment causes persisting periodic disturbances in the system. While power grids are designed to damp most of perturbations during standard operations, some of them can excite normal modes of the system and cause significant energy transfers across the system, creating large oscillations thousands of miles away from the source.

arxiv-2303-12073.title: 3D Mitochondria Instance Segmentation with Spatio-Temporal Transformers
arxiv-2303-12073.creator: Omkar Thawakar, Rao Muhammad Anwer, Jorma Laaksonen, Orly Reiner, Mubarak Shah, Fahad Shahbaz Khan
arxiv-2303-12073.description: Abstract Accurate 3D mitochondria instance segmentation in electron microscopy (EM) is a challenging problem and serves as a prerequisite to empirically analyze their distributions and morphology. Most existing approaches employ 3D convolutions to obtain representative features. However, these convolution-based approaches struggle to effectively capture long-range dependencies in the volume mitochondria data, due to their limited local receptive field.

arxiv-2305-17582.title: Electroweak symmetry breaking by gravity arXiv: 2305.17582
arxiv-2305-17582.creator: Yuri Shtanov
arxiv-2305-17582.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Yuri Shtanov. We consider a simple scale-invariant action coupling the Higgs field to the metric scalar curvature R R and containing an R 2 R^{2} term that exhibits spontaneous breaking of scale invariance and electroweak symmetry. The coefficient of the R 2 R^{2} term in this case determines the self-coupling of the Higgs boson in the Einstein frame, and the scalaron becomes a dilaton weakly coupled to the Higgs boson.

arxiv-2306-03452.title: Algebraic K-theory of reductive p p -adic groups
arxiv-2306-03452.creator: Bartels, A, Lück, W
arxiv-2306-03452.description: Abstract . Motivated by the Farrell–Jones Conjecture for group rings, we formulate the 𝒞 ​ op {\mathcal{C}\hskip-1.0pt\mathrm{op}} -Farrell–Jones Conjecture for the K-theory of Hecke algebras of td-groups. We prove this conjecture for (closed subgroups of) reductive p-adic groups G G .

arxiv-2406-09699.title: Differentiable Programming for Differential Equations: A Review
arxiv-2406-09699.creator: ndo Sapienza \email fsapienza@berkeley.edu, i Bolibar, k Schäfer, n Groenke, Pal, or Boussange, ick Heimbach, s Hooker, ando Pérez, Olof Persson, stopher Rackauckas
arxiv-2406-09699.description: Abstract The differentiable programming paradigm is a cornerstone of modern scientific computing. It refers to numerical methods for computing the gradient of a numerical model’s output. Many scientific models are based on differential equations, where differentiable programming plays a crucial role in calculating model sensitivities, inverting model parameters, and training hybrid models that combine differential equations with data-driven approaches.

arxiv-2507-07954.title: Input Conditioned Layer Dropping in Speech Foundation Models
arxiv-2507-07954.description: Abstract Curating foundation speech models for edge and IoT settings, where computational resources vary over time, requires dynamic architectures featuring adaptable reduction strategies. One emerging approach is layer dropping ( ℒ ​ 𝒟 \mathcal{LD} ) which skips fraction of the layers of a backbone network during inference to reduce the computational load. This allows transforming static models into dynamic ones.

arxiv-2509-03138.title: Suppression of dynamical momentum-space shell by chiral symmetry
arxiv-2509-03138.creator: Bikai Gao, Michał Marczenko
arxiv-2509-03138.description: Abstract We investigate the appearance of quark degrees of freedom in dense isospin-symmetric nuclear matter. We employ the parity doublet model to incorporate chiral dynamics. Specifically, we contrast quarkyonic matter, in which quarks occupy states above the nucleon Fermi surface, with baryquark matter, in which quarks populate states inside the nucleonic Fermi sea.

arxiv-2510-12808.title: REPRESENTING FINE SHAPE OF LOCAL COMPACTA BY HOMOTOPY CLASSES OF ORDINARY MAPS
arxiv-2510-12808.creator: VLADISLAV ZEMLYANOY
arxiv-2510-12808.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by VLADISLAV ZEMLYANOY. Fine shape, as defined by Melikhov, is an extension of the strong shape category of compacta (compact metrizable topological spaces) to all metrizable spaces, notable for being compatible with both Čech cohomology and Steenrod-Sitnikov homology.

arxiv-2510-24203.title: Fault-Tolerant Multiparty Session Types with Global Escape Loops
arxiv-2510-24203.creator: Lukas Bartl Julian Linne Kirstin Peters
arxiv-2510-24203.description: Abstract Multiparty session types are designed to abstractly capture the structure of communication protocols and verify behavioural properties. One important such property is progress, i.e., the absence of deadlock. Distributed algorithms often resemble multiparty communication protocols. But proving their properties, in particular termination that is closely related to progress, can be elaborate.

europmc-pmc3084176.creator: Russell TL, Govella NJ, Azizi S, Drakeley CJ, Kachur SP, Killeen GF.
europmc-pmc3084176.description: Background Insecticide-treated nets (ITNs) and indoor residual spraying (IRS) represent the front-line tools for malaria vector control globally, but are optimally effective where the majority of baseline transmission occurs indoors. In the surveyed area of rural southern Tanzan

pmc-10572573.title: Molecular Mechanisms of Resistance to Direct-Acting Antiviral (DAA) Drugs for the Treatment of Hepatitis C Virus Infections
pmc-10572573.creator: Mohammad Asrar Izhari, Chenhua Liu
pmc-10572573.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Hepatitis C virus (HCV) is a hepatotropic virus that affects millions of human lives worldwide. Direct-acting antiviral (DAA) regimens are the most effective HCV treatment option. However, amino acid substitution-dependent resistance to DAAs has been a major challenge. This study aimed to determine the increasing risk of DAA resistance due to substitutions in DAA target non-structural proteins (NS3/4A, NS5A, and NS5B).

pmc-10594807.title: Secoisolariciresinol diglucoside regulates estrogen receptor expression to ameliorate OVX-induced osteoporosis
pmc-10594807.creator: Guofang Chen, Yansong Chen, Junyi Hong, Junwei Gao, Zhikun Xu
pmc-10594807.description: ObjectiveSecoisolariciresinol diglucoside (SDG) is a phytoestrogen that has been reported to improve postmenopausal osteoporosis (PMOP) caused by estrogen deficiency. In our work, we aimed to investigate the mechanism of SDG in regulating the expressions of ERs on PMOP model rats.MethodsOvariectomization (OVX) was used to establish PMOP model in rats.

pmc-10682870.title: Incidence, mortality, and predictors of acute kidney injury in patients with heart failure: a systematic review
pmc-10682870.creator: Song‐Chao Ru, Shu‐Bin Lv, Zhi‐Juan Li
pmc-10682870.description: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is common in patients with heart failure (HF), but studies have been inconsistent about the incidence of AKI in patients with HF. We conducted a meta‐analysis to examine the incidence of AKI and its impact on mortality in patients with HF.

pmc-11377058.title: The genetics of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
pmc-11377058.creator: Melissa Nijs, Philip Van Damme
pmc-11377058.description: Purpose of reviewAmyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) has a strong genetic basis, but the genetic landscape of ALS appears to be complex. The purpose of this article is to review recent developments in the genetics of ALS.Recent findingsLarge-scale genetic studies have uncovered more than 40 genes contributing to ALS susceptibility.

pmc-12358339.title: Inter-reader agreement and additive benefit of SPECT or SPECT/CT modality with [99mTc]Tc-pertechnetate scintigraphy imaging for the assessment of thyroid nodules in a tertiary care center
pmc-12358339.creator: Emil Novruzov, Dominik Schmitt, Katalin Mattes-György, Julian Kuhlmann, Mareike Muchalla, Matthias Schott, Christina Antke, Frederik L Giesel, Eduards Mamlins
pmc-12358339.description: Aim/introductionIn central Europe, up to 76% of population exhibit thyroid nodules (TN). The combination of ultrasound findings and thyroid scan imaging are supposed to ensure a cost-effective and reliable prediction of malignancy risk. However, real-world impact of ultrasound findings, i.e. TI-RADS, has raised concerns due to its highly limited reliability and reproducibility.

pmc-12646454.title: Prediction method for the reaction force of vehicle door sealing systems
pmc-12646454.creator: Zhong Yang, Luoxing Li, Jing Huang, Guoqing Chen, Zhengqing Liu, Zhenhu Wang, Cebastien Joel Guembou Shouop, Cebastien Joel Guembou Shouop, Cebastien Joel Guembou Shouop
pmc-12646454.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The accuracy of calculating the reaction force in vehicle sealing systems using moment equilibrium equations from statics is highly dependent on the degree of simplification in the mathematical model. This study demonstrates that employing the Finite Element (FE) method allows for a comprehensive consideration of the coupling effects between the door and the flexible seal, thereby eliminating errors inherent to model simplification and single-boundary variables. Consequently, this approach improves the prediction accuracy of the sealing system’s reaction force.

pmc-13574604.title: Predicting clinically significant medication errors: Development and validation of a risk stratification model using incident reporting data
pmc-13574604.creator: Saad M. Wali, Nawaf S. Alqurashi, Malaz J. Gazzaz, Sharaf E. Sharaf, Maan H. Harbi, Fahad J. Alqahtani, Ohood K. Almuzaini, Eman O. Alsheikh, Saleh A. Almarshad, Sahar A. Abduljawad, Mohammed M. Aldurdunji
pmc-13574604.description: BackgroundMedication error reporting systems capture large volumes of incidents, yet only a small proportion lead to clinically significant patient outcomes. Distinguishing these high-risk errors from the majority of low-impact events remains a major challenge for healthcare systems. This study aimed to develop a predictive model to identify medication errors at elevated risk of clinical significance in a tertiary care setting.

pmc-13583152.title: Human Wharton’s Jelly Mesenchymal Stem Cells Improve Insulin Levels and Reduce Weight Gain in Aging Female Rats
pmc-13583152.creator: Wining Astini, Alif Iman Fitrianto, Adkhilni Utami, Adisti Dwijayanti, Frans Dyanagiri Suyatna, Adi Winarto, Arief Boediono
pmc-13583152.description: Background: This study aimed to analyze the effect of repeated intravenous injections of human Wharton's jelly mesenchymal stem cells (hWJ-MSCs), administered at a dose of 1 × 10⁶ cells/kg four times at 3-month intervals, on insulin levels and weight gain in aging female rats.

pmc-13603764.title: DDH-Net: A Graf-Compliant Method for Computer-Aided Assessment Using Infant Hip Ultrasound
pmc-13603764.creator: Xinyu Zhang, Jianwei Cui, Yuxiang Dai, Wenyi Zhang
pmc-13603764.description: Ultrasound assessment of developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH) in infants is highly operator-dependent, particularly during standard plane acquisition and Graf angle measurement. This paper proposes DDH-Net, a fully automated computer-aided assessment method for infant hip ultrasound that follows the complete Graf workflow.

pmc-13658438.title: Forensic facial approximation methodologies applied to the Brazilian population: a scoping review
pmc-13658438.creator: Paula de Sousa Rachid, Daniel Pignatari Mahet Rodrigues, Lucas Alves Jural, Andrea Vaz Braga Pintor, Lucianne Cople Maia, Antônio Carlos de Oliveira Ruellas, Maria Augusta Visconti, Andreia Cristina Breda de Souza
pmc-13658438.description: This scoping review aimed to map forensic facial approximation (FFA) methodologies applied to the Brazilian population. The protocol was registered in the Open Science Framework and adopted the following structure: Population, human; Concept, FFA methodologies; and Context, studies conducted in the Brazilian population. Searches were conducted in seven databases and grey literature up to December 2025.
